This document has been published in the Federal Register. Use the PDF linked in the document sidebar for the official electronic format.
The staff of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC or Commission) has prepared an environmental assessment (EA) for the Viola Project, proposed by Southern Star Central Gas Pipeline, Inc. (Southern Star) in the above-referenced docket.[1]
Southern Star requests authorization to construct a new meter station, flow station, compressor station, and the 19.3-mile-long 16-inch-diameter Line UA natural gas pipeline in Sumner County, Kansas. The Viola Project would provide up to 116,296 dekatherms per day of natural gas service to the planned 710-megwatt combined cycle power generation Viola Plant located in Sumner County, Kansas, which is owned and operated by Evergy, Inc. (Evergy).
Any person wishing to comment on the EA may do so. To ensure consideration of your comments on the proposal prior to making a decision on the project, it is important that the Commission receive your comments on or before 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time on November 9, 2026. Instructions for filing comments are provided on page 3.
FERC is the lead federal agency for authorizing interstate natural gas transmission facilities under the Natural Gas Act of 1938 and the lead federal agency for preparation of the EA. The EA assesses the potential environmental effects of the Viola Project in accordance with the requirements of the National Environmental Policy Act [2]
and the Commission's implementing regulations.[3]
The principal purposes of the EA are to: identify and assess the potential effects on the natural and human environment; describe and evaluate reasonable alternatives; identify and recommend mitigation measures; and facilitate public involvement in the environmental review process. The EA concludes that approval of the proposed project would not constitute a major federal action significantly affecting the quality of the human environment.
The EA addresses the potential environmental effects of the construction and operation of the following project facilities:
approximately 19.3 miles of new 16-inch-diameter natural gas pipeline (Line UA), which would connect to Southern Star's existing 20-inch-diamter Line U;
the new Wellington Compressor Station, sited along existing Line U, consisting of three compressor units totaling 12,375 horsepower, along with ancillary station equipment;
the Evergy Flow Control Setting, to regulate the flow of natural gas from existing Line U; and
the Evergy Meter Setting, which would connect Line UA to the new Evergy Viola Plant.
The Commission mailed a copy of the
Notice of Availability
of the EA to federal, state, and local government representatives and agencies; elected officials; Native American tribes; environmental and public interest groups; potentially affected landowners and other interested individuals and groups; and libraries and media outlets in the project area. The EA is only available in electronic format. It may be viewed and downloaded from the FERC's website (
www.ferc.gov), on the natural gas environmental documents page (
https://www.ferc.gov/industries-data/natural-gas/environment/environmental-documents). In addition, the EA may be accessed by using the eLibrary link on the FERC's website. Click on the eLibrary link (
https://elibrary.ferc.gov/eLibrary/search), select “General Search” and enter the docket number in the “Docket Number” field, excluding the last three digits (
i.e., CP26-74). Be sure you have selected an appropriate date range. For assistance, please contact FERC Online Support at
FercOnlineSupport@ferc.gov
or toll free at (866) 208-3676, or for TTY, contact (202) 502-8659.
The EA is not a decision document. It presents Commission staff's independent analysis of the
( printed page 65542)
environmental issues for the Commission to consider when addressing the merits of all issues in this proceeding. Under section 7(c) of the Natural Gas Act, the Commission determines whether interstate natural gas transportation facilities are in the public convenience and necessity and, if so, grants a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity to construct and operate them. The Commission bases its decisions on both economic issues, including need, and environmental effects.
Your comments should focus on the EA's disclosure and discussion of potential environmental effects, reasonable alternatives, and measures to avoid or lessen environmental effects. The more specific your comments, the more useful they will be. For your convenience, there are three methods you can use to file your comments to the Commission. The Commission encourages electronic filing of comments and has staff available to assist you at (866) 208-3676 or
FercOnlineSupport@ferc.gov. Please carefully follow these instructions so that your comments are properly recorded.
(1) You can file your comments electronically using the eComment feature on the Commission's website (
www.ferc.gov) under the link to FERC Online. This is an easy method for submitting brief, text-only comments on a project;
(2) You can also file your comments electronically using the eFiling feature on the Commission's website (
www.ferc.gov) under the link to FERC Online. With eFiling, you can provide comments in a variety of formats by attaching them as a file with your submission. AGENCY:
Public Buildings Reform Board.
ACTION:
Notice of public meeting.
SUMMARY:
As provided by the Federal Assets Sale and Transfer Act of 2016 (FASTA), the Public Buildings Reform Board (PBRB) is holding its fourteenth public meeting. At this meeting, the Board will discuss the progress of past rounds and well as plans for a future round.
DATES:
The meeting is scheduled for Tuesday, December 8, 2026 at 11:00 a.m. Eastern.
ADDRESSES:
The meeting will be held at the Arena Stage at the Mead Center for American Theater, 1101 6th Street SW, Washington, DC 20024.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
Paul Walden, PBRB, at (202) 716-8165, or questions and comments can be forwarded to the PBRB team at
fastainfo@pbrb.gov.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
Background:
FASTA created the PBRB as an independent Board to identify opportunities for the Federal government to significantly reduce its inventory of civilian real property and thereby reduce costs. The Board, to date, has submitted three rounds of recommendations. The Thomas R. Carper Water Resources Development Act of 2024 (WRDA) extended the Board to December 31, 2026 and allows for the submission of one additional round of recommendations (Round 3).
Format and Registration:
The format for the meeting will be panel discussions with appropriate time allowed for a Q&A segment. Participants may also view the meeting virtually. Interested participants must register for the public meeting via this link:
https://PBRBHearing14.eventbrite.com.
Individuals wishing to attend who require special assistance or
( printed page 65609)
accommodations must contact the PBRB Team at
fastainfo@pbrb.gov
at least 12 days prior to the event.
Portions of the meeting may be held in executive session if the Board is considering issues involving classified or proprietary information.
A transcript of the public meeting will be uploaded to
pbrb.gov
shortly after the session.

articles.full_text: In compliance with the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (PRA), this notice announces that the Information Collection Request (ICR) summarized below will be submitted to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for review and approval. The ICR describes the nature of the information collection and its expected burden. This document describes a collection of information for which NHTSA intends to seek OMB approval to evaluate driver's acceptance and use of intelligent speed assistance systems. A Federal Register Notice with a 60-day comment period soliciting comments on the following information collection was published on June 25, 2026. Five comments were received during the comment period. NHTSA has addressed these comments, and there are no resulting changes to this collection based on the comments. However, due to rounding adjustments, the total estimated burden hours were reduced from 311 to 308 hours.

articles.full_text:
AGENCY:
Nuclear Regulatory Commission.
                    SUMMARY:
The U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) is providing public notice each week, for four consecutive weeks, beginning October 1, 2026, of receipt and availability of the first part of a phased construction permit application, including a limited work authorization (LWA) request, from SMR, LLC, on behalf of Palisades SMR, LLC, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Holtec International (collectively, Holtec), for a dual-unit SMR-300 plant located at the Palisades Energy Center (PEC) in Covert, Michigan. The units are individually named Pioneer Unit 1 and Pioneer Unit 2. This is the third of four consecutive weekly notifications.
                    ADDRESSES:
Please refer to Docket ID NRC-2026-0265 when contacting the NRC about the availability of information regarding this document. You may obtain publicly available information related to this document using any of the following methods:
- Federal Rulemaking Website:
                         Go to 
                        https://www.regulations.gov
                         and search for Docket ID NRC-2026-0265. Address questions about Docket IDs in 
                        Regulations.gov
                         to Bridget Curran; telephone: 301-415-1003; email: 
                        Bridget.Curran@nrc.gov. For technical questions, contact the individual(s) listed in the 
                        FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT
                         section of this document.
                    
- NRC's Agencywide Documents Access and Management System (ADAMS):
                         You may obtain publicly available documents online in the ADAMS Public Documents collection at 
                        https://www.nrc.gov/reading-rm/adams.html. To begin the search, select “Begin ADAMS Public Search.” For problems with ADAMS, please contact the NRC's Public Document Room (PDR) reference staff at 1-800-397-4209, at 301-415-4737, or by email to 
                        PDR.Resource@nrc.gov. The Pioneer Units 1 and 2 LWA application is available in ADAMS under Package Accession No. ML25365A983.
                    
- NRC's PDR:
                         The PDR, where you may examine and order copies of publicly available documents, is open by appointment. To make an appointment to visit the PDR, please send an email to 
                        PDR.Resource@nrc.gov
                         or call 1-800-397-4209 or 301-415-4737, between 8 a.m. and 4 p.m. eastern time (ET), Monday through Friday, except Federal holidays.
                    
            
                SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
I. Discussion
                    On December 31, 2025, SMR, LLC, on behalf of Palisades SMR, LLC, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Holtec International (collectively, Holtec), filed with the NRC, the first part (Part 1) of a phased construction permit application for a utilization facility pursuant to Section 103 of the Atomic Energy Act and part 50 of title 10 of the 
                    Code of Federal Regulations
                     (10 CFR), “Domestic Licensing of Production and Utilization Facilities.” Part 1 of the application includes a LWA request pursuant to 10 CFR 50.10(d), “Request for limited work authorization”; three exemption requests; and a comprehensive environmental report (ER). In its LWA request, Holtec seeks NRC approval to conduct certain early construction activities of a dual-unit SMR-300 plant at the PEC in Covert, Michigan. Holtec also states that the comprehensive ER addresses the environmental impacts associated with LWA activities (including the requested exemptions), the remainder of construction to complete the plant, and plant operations. Holtec submitted Part 1 of its application as part of a phased application approach for a construction permit for a utilization facility, as described in 10 CFR 2.101(a)(9) and 10 CFR 2.600(d).
                
                    On February 27, 2026, the NRC issued a 
                    Federal Register
                     notice (91 FR 9892) stating that the NRC staff accepted Part 1 of the phased construction permit application for docketing and will perform a detailed technical review. These weekly notices of receipt and availability of the application are being provided in accordance with the requirements in 10 CFR 50.43(a)(3).
                
                    Authority:42 U.S.C. 2011 
                    et seq.
                    Dated: October 5, 2026.
For the Nuclear Regulatory Commission.
Michelle Hayes,
Chief, Advanced Reactor Licensing Branch 2, Division of Advanced Reactor Licensing, Office of Advanced Reactors.

AGENCY:
Enforcement and Compliance, International Trade Administration, Department of Commerce.
SUMMARY:
On October 2, 2026, the U.S. Court of International Trade (CIT) issued its final judgment in
Ellwood City Forge Company
v.
United State
s, Court no. 23-00191, sustaining the U.S. Department of Commerce (Commerce)'s first remand results pertaining to the administrative review of the antidumping duty (AD) order on forged steel fluid end blocks (FEBs) from Italy covering the period of review (POR) July 23, 2020 through December 31, 2021. Commerce is notifying the public that the CIT's final judgment is not in harmony with Commerce's final results of the administrative review, and that Commerce is amending the final results with respect to the dumping margin assigned to Lucchini Mame Forge S.p.A.
DATES:
Applicable October 12, 2026.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
Yang Jin Chun, AD/CVD Operations, Office I, Enforcement and Compliance, International Trade Administration, U.S. Department of Commerce, 1401 Constitution Avenue NW, Washington, DC 20230; telephone: (202) 482-5760.
( printed page 65528)
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
Background
On August 14, 2023, Commerce published its
Final Results
of the administrative review of the antidumping duty order on forged steel fluid end blocks from Italy covering the POR July 23, 2020 through December 31, 2021. Commerce calculated a weighted-average dumping margin of 2.97 percent.[1]
Elwood City Forge Company appealed Commerce's
Final Results.
On April 28, 2026, the CIT remanded the
Final Results
to Commerce, directing Commerce to: (1) further explain its determination that Cogne and Ciscato, two producers whose financial statements Commerce used to calculate Lucchini's CV profit, produced merchandise identical to the subject FEBs; and (2) further explain/reconsider its selection of the market-price benchmark used in the major input analysis.[2]
In its final results of redetermination, issued in July 2026, Commerce reversed both determinations. Commerce excluded Cogne and Ciscato from its CV profit calculation. Commerce also used Company A's U.S. purchases of ingots as the market-price benchmark for its major-input analysis and rejected Lucchini's February 2023 adjustment information as untimely new factual information.[3]
The CIT sustained Commerce's
Final Results of Redetermination.[4]
Timken Notice
In its decision in
Timken,[5]
as clarified by
Diamond Sawblades,[6]
the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit held that, pursuant to section 516A(c) and (e) of the Tariff Act of 1930, as amended (the Act), Commerce must publish a notice of court decision that is not “in harmony” with a Commerce determination and must suspend liquidation of entries pending a “conclusive” court decision. The CIT's October 2, 2026, judgment constitutes a final decision of the CIT that is not in harmony with Commerce's
Final Results.
Thus, this notice is published in fulfillment of the publication requirements of
Timken.
Amended Final Results
Because there is now a final court judgment, Commerce is amending its
Final Results
with respect to Lucchini as follows:
Exporter/producer
Final results
weighted-average
dumping margin
(percent)
Amended final results

(percent)
Lucchini Mame Forge S.p.A

Cash Deposit Requirements
Because Lucchini has a superseding cash deposit rate,
i.e.,
there have been final results published in a subsequent administrative review,[7]
we will not issue revised cash deposit instructions to U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP). This notice will not affect the current cash deposit rate.
Liquidation of Suspended Entries
At this time, Commerce remains enjoined by CIT order from liquidating entries that: were produced and/or exported by Lucchini, and were entered, or withdrawn from warehouse, for consumption during the period of review July 23, 2020, through December 31, 2021. These entries will remain enjoined pursuant to the terms of the injunction during the pendency of any appeals process.
In the event the CIT's ruling is not appealed, or, if appealed, upheld by a final and conclusive court decision, Commerce intends to instruct CBP to assess antidumping duties on unliquidated entries of subject merchandise produced and/or exported by Lucchini in accordance with 19 CFR 351.212(b). We will instruct CBP to assess antidumping duties on all appropriate entries covered by this review when the importer-specific
ad valorem
assessment rate is not zero or
de minimis.
Where an import-specific
ad valorem
assessment rate is zero or
de minimis,[8]
we will instruct CBP to liquidate the appropriate entries without regard to antidumping duties.
Notification to Interested Parties
This notice is issued and published in accordance with sections 516A(c) and (e) and 777(i)(1) of the Act.
Dated: October 9, 2026.
Scot Fullerton,
Acting Deputy Assistant Secretary for Antidumping and Countervailing Duty Operations.

AGENCY:
Enforcement and Compliance, International Trade Administration, Department of Commerce.
SUMMARY:
The U.S. Department of Commerce (Commerce) preliminarily determines that Oman Fasteners LLC (Oman Fasteners) did not make sales of the subject merchandise at less than normal value (NV) during the period of review (POR), July 1, 2024, through June 30, 2025. In addition, we intend to rescind the review with respect to 15 companies. Interested parties are invited to comment on these preliminary results of review.
DATES:
Applicable October 15, 2026.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
Catherine Bonilla, AD/CVD Operations, Office OIV, Enforcement and
( printed page 65529)
Compliance, International Trade Administration, U.S. Department of Commerce, 1401 Constitution Avenue NW, Washington, DC 20230; telephone: (202) 482-7955.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
Background
On August 22, 2025, based on timely requests for review, in accordance with 19 CFR 351.221(c)(1)(i), we initiated an administrative review of the antidumping duty (AD) order on certain steel nails (steel nails) from Sultanate of Oman (Oman).[1]
On September 22, 2025, we selected Oman Fasteners for individual examination as the sole mandatory respondent in this review.[2]
Due to the lapse in appropriations and Federal Government shutdown, on November 14, 2025, Commerce tolled all deadlines in administrative proceedings by 47 days.[3]
Additionally, due to a backlog of documents that were electronically filed via Enforcement and Compliance's Antidumping and Countervailing Duty Centralized Electronic Service System (ACCESS) during the Federal Government shutdown, on November 24, 2025, Commerce tolled all deadlines in administrative proceedings by an additional 21 days.[4]
On May 20, 2026, Commerce extended the deadline for the preliminary results of this administrative review by 113 days.[5]
On September 29, 2026, Commerce further extended the deadline for the preliminary results for an additional 7 days.[6]
The deadline for the preliminary results is now October 7, 2026.
For a complete description of the events that followed the initiation of this review,
See
the Preliminary Decision Memorandum.[7]
A list of the topics discussed in the Preliminary Decision Memorandum is attached as Appendix I to this notice. The Preliminary Decision Memorandum is a public document and is on file electronically via ACCESS, which is available to registered users at
https://access.trade.gov.
In addition, a complete version of the Preliminary Decision Memorandum can be accessed at
https://access.trade.gov/frnotices.
Scope of the Order
The merchandise subject to the
Order
is steel nails from Oman. For a complete description of the scope of the
Order, see
the Preliminary Decision Memorandum.
Intent To Rescind Administrative Review, In Part
It is Commerce's practice to rescind an administrative review of a duty order, pursuant to 19 CFR 351.213(d)(3), when there are no reviewable entries of subject merchandise during the POR for which liquidation is suspended. Normally, upon completion of an administrative review, the suspended entries are liquidated at the AD assessment rate calculated for the POR.[8]
Therefore, for an administrative review of a company to be conducted, there must be a reviewable, suspended entry that Commerce can instruct U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) to liquidate at the AD assessment rate calculated for the POR.[9]
According to the CBP import data on the record, the companies listed in Appendix II subject to this review did not have reviewable entries of subject merchandise during the POR for which liquidation is suspended.[10]
Accordingly, in the absence of reviewable, suspended entries of subject merchandise during the POR, we intend to rescind this administrative review with respect to these companies listed in Appendix II, in accordance with 19 CFR 351.213(d)(3).
Methodology
Commerce is conducting this review in accordance with section 751(a) of the Tariff Act of 1930, as amended (the Act). Export price is calculated in accordance with section 772 of the Act. NV is calculated in accordance with section 773 of the Act. For a full description of the methodology underlying our conclusions,
see
the Preliminary Decision Memorandum.
The Act and Commerce's regulations do not address the establishment of a rate to be applied to companies not selected for individual examination when Commerce limits its examination in an administrative review pursuant to section 777A(c)(2) of the Act. Generally, Commerce looks to section 735(c)(5) of the Act, which provides instructions for calculating the all-others rate in a market economy investigation, for guidance when calculating the rate for companies which were not selected for individual examination in an administrative review. Under section 735(c)(5)(A) of the Act, the all-others rate is normally “an amount equal to the weighted average of the estimated weighted average dumping margins established for exporters and producers individually investigated, excluding any zero or
de minimis
margins, and any margins determined entirely {on the basis of facts available}.”
Rate for Non-Examined Company
The SAA provides Commerce with additional guidance as to what the agency should do when the only margins calculated for individually-investigated exporters are zero/
de minimis
and/or determined entirely through facts available:
In such situations, Commerce may use any reasonable method to calculate the all others rate. The expected method in such cases will be to weight-average the zero and
de minimis
margins and margins determined pursuant to the facts available, provided that volume data is available. However, if this method is not feasible, or if it results in an average that would not be reasonably reflective of potential dumping margins for non-investigated exporters or producers, Commerce may use other reasonable methods.[11]
In this review, we preliminary calculated a dumping margin of zero percent for Oman Fasteners, the sole respondent individually examined. Therefore, there is no non-zero weighted-average dumping margin established for exporters and producers individually examined in this POR. Further, Oman Fasteners the only producer and/or exporter with a history of individual examination in this
Order,
and the non-individually examined respondent under review, Gulf Nails LLC, has no history of individual review. articles.title: Wilkes-Barre Terminal Railway Company-Acquisition and Operation Exemption-Luzerne County Redevelopment Authority and Luzerne County Rail Corporation
articles.full_text:
Wilkes-Barre Terminal Railway Company (WBT), a noncarrier, has filed a verified notice of exemption under 49 CFR 1150.31 to acquire approximately 59.65 miles of rail line (the Line) from the Luzerne County Redevelopment Authority (LCRA) and the operating rights from LCRA's non-operating subsidiary Luzerne County Rail Corporation (LCRC), in Luzerne County, Pa. The Line consists of the following in-service segments: (1) the Dunmore Secondary Track, between milepost 6.5, at Avoca, Pa., and milepost 10+/− North side Montage Road Crossing, a distance of 4.5 miles; [] 
                    
                     (2) the Avoca Industrial Track, between milepost 1.8, at Number 7 Junction, and milepost 6.5, at Avoca, a distance of 4.7 miles,[] 
                    
                     including the connection with the track of Reading Blue Mountain & Northern Railroad Company (RBMN) between LB Junction and the switch of the Dunmore Secondary Track, a distance of 0.123 miles, and the Langcliff Connecting Track, between milepost 0.0, at Duryea, Pa., and the connection with Norfolk Southern Railway in the middle of York Avenue, at milepost 0.867, a distance of 0.867 miles; (3) the Suscon Industrial Track, between milepost 154.5, at Suscon, Pa., and milepost 158.7, at Hillside, Pa., a distance of 4.2 miles; (4) the Wilkes-Barre Secondary, between milepost 169.2, at Ashley, Pa., and milepost 185.5, at Pittston, Pa., a distance of 16.3 miles; (5) the GWBP Industrial Track, between milepost 0.0, at Ashley, and milepost 0.5, at Hanover Industrial Track, a distance of 0.5 miles; (6) the Brownsville Industrial Track, between milepost 0.0, at Hillside, and milepost 1.0, at Brownsville, Pa., a distance of 1.0 miles; (7) the Wilkes-Barre Industrial Track, between milepost 59.9, at Ferry Street, and milepost 62.9, at Wilkes-Barre, Pa., a distance of 3.0 miles; (8) the Kingston Industrial Track, between milepost 142.7, at Pittston Junction, and Railroad Station 8594+58, a distance of 8.1 miles; and (9) the D&H Wilkes-Barre Connector, from milepost A-208.08, Hudson Yard, to Conyngham Avenue, City of Wilkes-Barre, Pa., a distance of 2.5 miles; and (10) the APC line, between milepost 0.0 and 0.6 in Wilkes-Barre, a distance of 0.6 miles.
                
                    The Line consists of the following out-of-service segments: (1) the West Pittston Running Track, between milepost 0.0, at West Pittston, Pa., and milepost 3.0, at Harding, Pa., a distance of 3.0 miles, and between milepost 186.4, at West Pittston, and milepost 190.2, at Wyoming, Pa., a distance of 3.8 miles, and between milepost 194.2, at Wyoming, and milepost 194.4, in Kingston, Pa., a distance of 0.2 miles; (2) the Nanticoke Industrial Track, between milepost 0.0, at Ashley, and milepost 2.6 at Central Scrap, a distance of 2.6 miles; (3) the Harry E. Breaker Spur, between milepost 0.1, at Maltby Junction, and milepost 0.5, a distance of 0.4 miles; (4) the Miner's Mills Industrial Track, between milepost 173.6, at North Wilkes-Barre, and milepost 176.1, at Hudson, Pa., a distance of 2.5 miles; and (5) the Pettibone Branch, between milepost 0.0 and milepost 0.759, at Dorranceton, Pa., a distance of 0.759 miles.[] 
                    
                
According to the verified notice, WBT will enter into an agreement with LCRA and LCRC for the acquisition of the Line and operating rights to ensure continued rail service to customers. According to the verified notice, WBT will grant local trackage rights to RBMN to provide immediate rail service to customers on the Line following the expiration of the incumbent operator's lease.
                    This transaction is related to a concurrently filed verified notice of exemption in 
                    Reading Blue Mountain & Northern Railroad—Trackage Rights Exemption—Wilkes-Barre Terminal Railway,
                     Docket No. FD 36959, in which RBMN seeks authority to acquire local trackage rights over the in-service segments of the Line.[] 
                    
                
According to WBT, the proposed transaction does not contain an interchange commitment. WBT certifies that its projected annual revenues resulting from the transaction will not exceed $5 million and will not result in WBT's becoming a Class I or Class II rail carrier.
The earliest this transaction may be consummated is October 29, 2026, the effective date of the exemption (30 days after the verified notice was filed).
If the verified notice contains false or misleading information, the exemption is void ab initio. Petitions to revoke the exemption under 49 U.S.C. 10502(d) may be filed at any time. The filing of a petition to revoke will not automatically stay the effectiveness of the exemption. Petitions for stay must be filed no later than October 22, 2026 (at least seven days before the exemption becomes effective).
All pleadings, referring to Docket No. FD 36958, must be filed with the Surface Transportation Board either via e-filing on the Board's website or in writing addressed to 395 E Street SW, Washington, DC 20423-0001. In addition, a copy of each pleading must be served on WBT's representative, Justin J. Marks, Clark Hill PLC, 601 13th Street NW, Suite 600, Washington, DC 20005.
According to WBT, this action is categorically excluded from environmental review under 49 CFR 1105.6(c) and from historic preservation reporting requirements under 49 CFR 1105.8(b).
                    Board decisions and notices are available at 
                    www.stb.gov.
                    Decided: October 9, 2026.
By the Board, Anika S. Cooper, Chief Counsel, Office of Chief Counsel
Kenyatta Clay,
Clearance Clerk.

articles.title: Fisheries of the Exclusive Economic Zone off Alaska; Pacific Ocean Perch in the Central Regulatory Area of the Gulf of Alaska
articles.summary: NMFS is prohibiting retention of the incidental catch allowance for Pacific Ocean perch in the Central Regulatory Area of the Gulf of Alaska (GOA) except by vessels checked-in to the Central GOA Rockfish Program who are fishing with a rockfish cooperative quota permit. This action is necessary because the 2026 total allowable catch (TAC) apportioned as the incidental catch allowance for Pacific Ocean perch in the Central GOA will soon be or has been reached.
articles.full_text:
AGENCY:
National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS), National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), Commerce.
                    ACTION:
Temporary rule; closure.
                    SUMMARY:
NMFS is prohibiting retention of the incidental catch allowance for Pacific Ocean perch in the Central Regulatory Area of the Gulf of Alaska (GOA) except by vessels checked-in to the Central GOA Rockfish Program who are fishing with a rockfish cooperative quota permit. This action is necessary because the 2026 total allowable catch (TAC) apportioned as the incidental catch allowance for Pacific Ocean perch in the Central GOA will soon be or has been reached.
                    DATES:
Effective 1200 hours, Alaska local time (A.l.t.), October 14, 2026, through 2400 hours, A.l.t., December 31, 2026.
            
                SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
NMFS manages the groundfish fishery in the GOA exclusive economic zone according to the Fishery Management Plan for Groundfish of the GOA (FMP) prepared and recommended by the North Pacific Fishery Management Council under authority of the Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act (Magnuson-Stevens Act). Regulations governing fishing by U.S. vessels in accordance with the FMP appear at subpart H of 50 CFR part 600 and 50 CFR part 679.
The 2026 Pacific Ocean perch TAC apportioned as the incidental catch allowance in the Central Regulatory Area of the GOA for vessels other than vessels checked-in to the Central GOA Rockfish Program who are fishing with a rockfish cooperative quota permit is 2,800 metric tons as established by the final 2026 and 2027 harvest specifications for groundfish of the GOA (91 FR 11902, March 11, 2026).
The Regional Administrator, Alaska Region, NMFS (Regional Administrator) has determined that the 2026 TAC of Pacific Ocean perch apportioned as the incidental catch allowance for vessels other than vessels checked-in to the Central GOA Rockfish Program who are fishing with a rockfish cooperative quota permit will soon be or has been reached.
Therefore, in accordance with § 679.
20(d)(2), NMFS is prohibiting retention of the incidental catch allowance for Pacific Ocean perch for vessels in the Central Regulatory Area of the GOA other than vessels checked-in to the Central GOA Rockfish Program who are fishing with a rockfish cooperative quota permit and requiring that Pacific ocean perch in the Central Regulatory Area of the GOA be treated in the same manner as a prohibited species, as described under § 679.
21(a), for the remainder of the year, except for Pacific Ocean perch in the Central Regulatory Area of the GOA caught by catcher vessels using hook-and-line, pot, or jig gear as described in § 679.
20(j), or caught by catcher vessels using trawl gear participating in the electronic monitoring program as described in § 679.
21(a)(2).
This action is necessary to prevent exceeding the 2026 Pacific Ocean perch TAC apportioned as the incidental catch allowance in the Central Regulatory Area of the GOA.
This action does not apply to vessels checked-in to the Central GOA Rockfish Program who are fishing with a rockfish cooperative quota permit.
While this prohibition is effective the requirements of § 679.
20(j)(4) apply.

Classification
NMFS issues this action pursuant to section 305(d) of the Magnuson-Stevens Act. This action is required by 50 CFR part 679, which was issued pursuant to section 304(b) of the Magnuson-Stevens Act, and is exempt from review under Executive Order 12866.
Pursuant to 5 U.S.C. 553(b)(B), there is good cause to waive prior notice and an opportunity for public comment on this action, as notice and comment would be impracticable and contrary to the public interest, as it would prevent NMFS from responding to the most recent fisheries data in a timely fashion and would delay prohibiting the retention of Pacific Ocean perch apportioned as the incidental catch allowance in the Central Regulatory Area of the GOA. NMFS was unable to publish a notice providing time for public comment because the most recent, relevant data on the total catch of Pacific Ocean perch in the Central Regulatory Area of the GOA only became available as of October 13, 2026.
There is good cause under 5 U.S.C. 553(d)(3) to establish an effective date less than 30 days after date of publication. This finding is based upon the reasons provided above for waiver of prior notice and opportunity for public comment.
                    
                    
                        16 U.S.C. 1801 
                        et seq.
                
                    Dated: October 13, 2026.
Shannon Bettridge,
Acting Director, Office of Sustainable Fisheries, National Marine Fisheries Service.

AGENCY:
Office of Personnel Management.
ACTION:
Direct final rule.
SUMMARY:
The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) is issuing a direct final rule making technical revisions to OPM's Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) regulations to incorporate various statutory amendments. The rule reflects statutory changes making virtually all Federal civilian service and certain honorable active military service qualify for determining FMLA eligibility, making clear that annual and sick leave provided under an authority outside of title 5, United States Code, may be substituted for unpaid FMLA leave, and excluding certain Veterans Health Administration (VHA) employees from title 5 FMLA coverage.
DATES:
This rule is effective December 14, 2026, unless significant adverse comments are received by November 16, 2026. If significant adverse comments are received, OPM will withdraw the affected provisions of this rule and issue a notice of proposed rulemaking.
ADDRESSES:
You may submit comments for this direct final rule within the Federal eRulemaking Portal at
https://www.regulations.gov/.
Follow the instructions for submitting comments.
All comments must be received by the end of the comment period for them to be considered. All comments and other submissions received generally will be posted on the internet at
regulations.gov
as they are received, without change, including any personal information provided. However, OPM retains discretion to redact personal or sensitive information, including but not limited to personal or sensitive information pertaining to third parties.
A summary of this rule may be found in the docket for this rulemaking at
www.regulations.gov.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
Julie Ohr, Office of Personnel Management, Workforce Policy and Innovation, (202) 606-2858,
leavepolicy@opm.gov.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
This direct final rule amends OPM's Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) regulations in subpart L of part 630 of title 5, Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) to reflect statutory changes enacted in January 2021 [1]
and December 2023.[2]
I. Background and Effect on Paid Parental Leave
The Family and Medical Leave Act of 1993, as amended, provides eligible employees with unpaid, job-protected leave for specified family and medical reasons under one of two separate and independent authorities, known as title I and title II of the FMLA. Title II of the FMLA added a Family and Medical Leave subchapter V in chapter 63 of title 5 of the United States Code (5 U.S.C. chapter 63, subchapter V), so it is generally referred to as “title 5 FMLA.” Title 5 FMLA is administered by OPM and applies to most Federal employees who are covered by the Federal leave system under 5 U.S.C. chapter 63 and some additional categories of employees. Title I of FMLA (non-title 5 FMLA), administered by the Department of Labor (DOL), applies to private sector employees, State and local Government employees, as well as some Federal employees (including employees of the U.S. Postal Service and the Postal Regulatory Commission). DOL's FMLA regulations are found in 29 CFR part 825 and should not be applied to employees covered by title 5 FMLA.
The 2021 and 2023 statutory amendments to the title 5 FMLA law also affect an employee's eligibility for paid parental leave (PPL). This is because PPL is a type of paid leave that is substituted for unpaid FMLA leave. Therefore, to be eligible for PPL, an employee must meet all eligibility requirements for use of FMLA leave as a covered “employee” (as defined in 5 U.S.C. 6381(1)(A)) who has completed at least 12 months of qualifying service (as required by 5 U.S.C. 6381(1)(B)). On August 10, 2020, OPM issued interim final FMLA/PPL regulations (85 FR 48075) to implement the Federal Employee Paid Leave Act (FEPLA),[3]
which authorizes the substitution of up to 12 weeks of PPL for unpaid FMLA leave granted in connection with the birth of an employee's son or daughter or the placement of a son or daughter with an employee for adoption or foster care. (See 5 U.S.C. 6382(a)(1)(A) and (B).) To implement FEPLA, OPM added new regulatory subpart Q (Paid Parental Leave) in 5 CFR part 630 and made necessary clarifications, changes, and additions in subpart L (Family and Medical Leave). Because the 2021 and 2023 statutory amendments addressed in this rule affect FMLA eligibility, those amendments (and this rule) therefore also affect PPL eligibility.
The 2021 and 2023 statutory amendments to title 5 FMLA were enacted after the publication of OPM's interim final FMLA/PPL rule and have been implemented through policy guidance in two OPM memoranda to heads of agencies titled “Technical Amendments Related to Family and Medical Leave and Paid Parental Leave under Section 1103 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021” (CPM 2021-07, January 14, 2021) [4]
and “Amendment Related to Inclusion of Certain Military Active Service for Family and Medical Leave and Paid Parental Leave Eligibility Purposes under Section 1114 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024” (CPM 2024-05, February 13, 2024).[5]
The changes made in this direct final rule implement clear statutory requirements and codify the guidance found in those memoranda.
( printed page 65438)
II. January 2021 Statutory Amendments and Corresponding Regulatory Changes
1. The statutory amendment to section 6301(2)(v) changed the scope of employees excluded from coverage under the title 5 FMLA law. Before the amendment, section 6301(2)(v) provided that VHA physicians, dentists, and nurses in the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) were excluded from the title 5 annual and sick leave system, since they were covered by a leave system established under 38 U.S.C. 7421. However, the original title 5 FMLA law definition of “employee” (5 U.S.C. 6381(1)) expressly included these employees as covered by title 5 FMLA. While these employees were covered by the title 5 FMLA law, OPM's FMLA regulations provided that they would be covered by FMLA regulations prescribed by the VA Secretary (see 5 CFR 630.1201(b)(3)(i) and (4)), which were required to be consistent with the OPM regulations. AGENCY:
National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS), National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), Commerce.
ACTION:
Temporary rule; quota transfer.
SUMMARY:
NMFS is transferring 15 metric tons (mt) of Atlantic bluefin tuna (BFT) quota from the Reserve category to the Angling category large school/small medium subquota. This transfer results in an adjusted Angling category large school/small medium subquota of 188.4 mt and an adjusted Reserve category quota of 27 mt. This action is intended to provide further harvest opportunities for Angling category fishermen, based on consideration of the regulatory determination criteria regarding inseason adjustments and applies to HMS Angling and HMS Charter/Headboat permitted vessels when fishing recreationally for BFT.
DATES:
The quota transfer is effective October 13, 2026 through December 31, 2026.
Atlantic BFT fisheries are managed under the 2006 Consolidated HMS Fishery Management Plan (FMP) and its amendments, pursuant to the Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act (Magnuson-Stevens Act; 16 U.S.C. 1801et seq.) and consistent with the Atlantic Tunas Convention Act (ATCA; 16 U.S.C. 971et seq.). ATCA is the implementing statute for binding recommendations of the International Commission for the Conservation of Atlantic Tunas (ICCAT). The HMS FMP and its amendments are implemented by regulations at 50 CFR part 635. Section 635.27(a) divides the U.S. BFT quota, established by ICCAT and as implemented by the United States among the various domestic fishing categories, per the allocations established in the HMS FMP and its amendments. NMFS is required under the Magnuson-Stevens Act at 16 U.S.C. 1854(g)(1)(D) to provide U.S. fishing vessels with a reasonable opportunity to harvest quotas under relevant international fishery agreements such as the ICCAT Convention, which is implemented domestically pursuant to ATCA.
Every year, the BFT fishing year starts on January 1 and ends on December 31. The Angling category opens on January 1 and continues through December 31 or until the applicable quota or subquota is reached or projected to be reached, whichever comes first. NMFS recently published a final rule to implement the 2025 ICCAT recommendation 25-05 (91 FR 53526, August 19, 2026). As described in § 635.27(a), the current baseline U.S. BFT quota is 1,509.98 mt (not including the 62.5 mt ICCAT allocated to the United States to account for bycatch of BFT in pelagic longline fisheries in the vicinity of the management area boundary and adjacent areas per § 635.27(a)(3)). The baseline quotas for the Angling and Reserve categories are 341.3 mt (§ 635.27(a)(2)) and 43.8 mt (§ 635.27(a)(6)), respectively. The Angling category quota is further subdivided into subquotas by size class. Specific to this action, the subquotas are 157.2 mt for school BFT and 173.4 mt for large school/small medium BFT (
see
§ 635.27(a)(2) and (a)(2)(ii)). To date, NMFS has published several actions that have adjusted the Reserve category quota (91 FR 5855, February 10, 2026; 91 FR 43571, July 16, 2026; 91 FR 53526, August 19, 2026; 91 FR 64302, October 8, 2026). The current adjusted Reserve category quota is 42 mt.
Transfer From the Reserve Category to the Angling Category Large School/Small Medium Subquota
Under § 635.27(a)(8), NMFS has the authority to transfer quota among fishing categories or subcategories after considering the determination criteria provided under § 635.27(a)(7). This section focuses on the calculations involved in transferring quota currently available from the 2026 Reserve category to the 2026 Angling category quota; the consideration of the determination criteria can be found below after this section.
As stated above, the baseline Angling category large school/small medium subquota is 173.4 mt. The adjusted Reserve category quota is 42 mt. Transferring 15 mt from the Reserve category to the Angling category large school/small medium subquota results in an adjusted Angling category large school/small medium subquota of 188.4 mt (173.4 mt + 15 mt = 188.4 mt), and an adjusted Reserve category quota of 27 mt (42 mt−15 mt = 27 mt). With this transfer the overall Angling category quota increases to 356.3 mt (341.3 mt + 15 mt = 356.3 mt). The Angling category quota is available for use by HMS Angling and HMS Charter/Headboat permitted vessels when fishing recreationally for BFT.
In summary, this transfer results in an adjusted Angling category large school/small medium subquota of 188.4 mt and an adjusted Reserve quota of 27 mt. The Angling category large school/small medium fishery will remain open until December 31, 2026, or until the adjusted Angling category large school/small medium subquota is reached, whichever comes first.
Consideration of the Relevant Determination Criteria
NMFS has considered all of the relevant determination criteria and their applicability to these inseason actions (§ 635.27(a)(7)). These criteria include, but are not limited to, the following:
Regarding the usefulness of information obtained from catches in the particular category for biological sampling and monitoring of the status of the stock (§ 635.27(a)(7)(i)), biological samples collected from BFT landed by recreational fishermen continue to provide NMFS with valuable parts and data for ongoing scientific studies of BFT age and growth, migration, and reproductive status. Additional opportunity to land BFT in the Angling category would support the continued collection of a broad range of data for these studies and for stock monitoring purposes.
NMFS also considered the catches of the Angling category quota to date and the likelihood of closure of that segment of the fishery if no adjustment is made (§ 635.27(a)(7)(ii). In doing so, NMFS also reviewed the latest information regarding landings and the availability of BFT on the fishing grounds (§ 635.27(a)(7)(ix)). Fishery performance in recent years indicates that in the late summer/fall the recreational fishery shifts to large school/small medium-sized BFT as these sized fish are more geographically spread out along the east coast. A quota transfer at this time should provide additional opportunities to harvest the large school/small medium subquota while avoiding exceeding the overall Angling category quota. Should recreational landings be higher or lower than expected, NMFS could take another action later in the year to further adjust the daily retention limit or close the Angling category fishery.

SUMMARY:
The Federal Labor Relations Authority (FLRA) publishes this document to implement the vacatur of the interim final rule published March 24, 2026 (Interim Final Rule). Except for certain minor or technical changes that were part of the Interim Final Rule but were not vacated, this document reinstates the wording of the affected regulations as they appeared before the Interim Final Rule took effect.

This final rule is effective on October 15, 2026.

I. Background

Meaning of Terms as Used in This Subchapter; Representation Proceedings; National Consultation Rights and Consultation Rights on Government-wide Rules or Regulations; Miscellaneous and General Requirements, 91 FR 13933 (Mar. 24, 2026) (Member Anne Wagner dissenting). The Interim Final Rule was effective April 23, 2026.
Id.
at 13933. In a memorandum and order on June 29, 2026, the United States District Court for the District of Massachusetts held that the Interim Final Rule and its April 23, 2026, effective date were arbitrary and capricious.
See AFGE, AFL-CIO
v.
FLRA,
838 F.Supp.3d 90 (D. Mass. June 29, 2026). In a final judgment on July 8, 2026, the District Court vacated the Interim Final Rule, except for certain minor or technical changes that are discussed in Section II below.
See id.,
Final J., Dkt. No. 45 (D. Mass. July 8, 2026). In order to implement the District Court's vacatur, this document reinstates the wording of the affected regulations as they appeared before the Interim Final Rule took effect—except for the minor or technical changes that the vacatur did not affect. These reinstated regulations were already in effect as a matter of law due to the District Court's decision, but this publication restores their appearance in the
Code of Federal Regulations.
The FLRA has sought reconsideration of the District Court's decision. The FLRA will issue a superseding notice in the
Federal Register
if the District Court's decision is vacated.
II. Minor or Technical Changes
The Interim Final Rule's minor or technical changes that the District Court did not vacate are set forth in 5 CFR 2422.3; 2422.5; 2422.6; 2422.34; 2426.2(b)(2)(i), (iv), & (v), and (b)(3)(ii); 2426.12(b)(2)(i), (iv), & (v), and (b)(3)(ii); 2429.7; and 2929.24(f)(7) and (f)(9).
See id.
Because these revisions have remained unchanged since the Interim Final Rule's effective date, they are not changed in this final rule.

The FLRA has determined that there is good cause for dispensing with an opportunity for comment, inasmuch as this rule merely conforms the text in the
Code of Federal Regulations
to the requirements of the District Court's decision.
Additionally, the FLRA finds that providing notice and an opportunity to comment is unnecessary because the FLRA is simply conducting the ministerial task of implementing the final judgment of the District Court.
Further, the FLRA finds good cause to make the revisions immediately effective under § 553(d)(3) of the Administrative Procedure Act.

AGENCY:
Bureau of the Fiscal Service, Department of the Treasury.
ACTION:
Final rule.
SUMMARY:
The Department of the Treasury (“Treasury” or “we”) is issuing in final form amendments to the Uniform Offering Circular for the Sale and Issue of Marketable Book-Entry Treasury Bills, Notes, and Bonds (the “UOC” or “auction rules”). These amendments make technical changes to several sections of the UOC to remove outdated references and to be consistent with Treasury's current auction terminology. These amendments also modify the requirements for submitting noncompetitive customer bids, to require submitters to provide all
( printed page 65457)
customer bid information prior to the noncompetitive auction close.
DATES:
Effective date:
October 15, 2026.
Applicability Date:
The changes to 31 CFR 356.14 and 356.23 apply to all auctions of Treasury marketable securities beginning with the first Treasury marketable securities auction conducted using Treasury's upgraded auction system, which will be communicated to market participants in advance of the first applicable auction. All other changes apply as of the effective date.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
Lori Santamorena, Kevin Hawkins, John Garrison, or Luisa Jou-Penchev, Office of Securities Regulatory Operations, Office of Financing, at
govsecreg@fiscal.treasury.gov
or 202-504-3632.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
Background
The UOC, codified at 31 CFR part 356, sets out the terms and conditions for the sale and issuance by Treasury to the public of marketable book-entry Treasury bills, notes, and bonds.[1]
The UOC and the offering announcement for each auction represent a comprehensive statement of the auction terms and conditions.[2]
Discussion
In September 2026, Treasury announced plans to upgrade the auction system for the sale of marketable Treasury securities.[3]
In connection with the planned upgrade, Treasury is adopting amendments to the UOC to align auction rules with the planned system upgrades and to make other technical amendments for clarity and consistency.
First, Treasury is modifying the definitions of adjusted value, dated date, index ratio, issue date, and settlement amount in § 356.2 and making conforming changes to the examples in appendix B to part 356 with respect to references to dated date, issue date, and original issue date. The changes include a clarification that the denominator in the formula for calculating the index ratio is always the reference Consumer Price Index applicable for the original dated date. None of the changes affect the calculation of the adjusted value, index ratio, or settlement amount for inflation-protected securities.
Second, Treasury is making several changes to remove outdated references, by modifying (1) the definition of CUSIP number in § 356.2 to remove a reference to the name of the entity that formerly issued CUSIPs; (2) § 356.11(a)(2) to remove a reference to bids in paper form, which are no longer accepted; and (3) the header to Section III of appendix B to part 356 to remove a reference to inflation-indexed securities, which are now uniformly referred to as inflation-protected securities.
Third, Treasury is modifying the definitions of index, index rate, and noncompetitive bid in § 356.2, and modifying §§ 356.15, 356.20, and 356.21 to align references to the high yield, high discount rate, or high discount margin more closely to Treasury's current auction terminology. We are also modifying §§ 356.20 and 356.23 to use the words award and recognize in lieu of accept and tender. Section 356.23(b) is also revised to clarify that the list of information that may be included in the auction results is illustrative. These changes improve consistency between the auction rules, announcements, and results. Treasury will make corresponding adjustments to the terminology on future auction announcements and results press releases, as appropriate.
Fourth, Treasury is modifying the requirements for submitting noncompetitive customer bids in §§ 356.14(c) and (e) to require submitters to provide, prior to the noncompetitive auction close, each individual customer's name and bid amount for all noncompetitive bids. Submitters will no longer be able to submit a summary bid amount; the individual customer names and respective bid amounts may still be submitted in one consolidated list, but it must be received prior to the noncompetitive auction close. These changes, which will be effective with the planned system upgrades, will ensure all noncompetitive bid information is received prior to the noncompetitive auction close and will enable Treasury auction staff to finalize post-auction operations earlier in the day.
Finally, Treasury is removing references in §§ 356.23(a) and 356.31(a) to
http://www.treasurydirect.gov
and instead stating that we will make the auction results available on our website. This change will provide Treasury more administrative flexibility while maintaining public transparency regarding auction results.
Administrative Procedure Act (APA).
The APA generally imposes requirements on agency rulemakings related to notice, public comment, and delayed effective dates, under 5 U.S.C. 553. However, 5 U.S.C. 553(a)(2) exempts matters relating to contracts from those requirements. The auction regulations relate to Treasury securities, which are contracts between Treasury and the owner of the security; therefore, the notice, public comment, and delayed effective date requirements of the APA do not apply to this final rule.
Regulatory Flexibility Act.
The provisions of the Regulatory Flexibility Act, 5 U.S.C. 601et seq.,
do not apply to this final rule because, pursuant to 5 U.S.C. 553(a)(2), this rule is not required to be issued with notice and opportunity for public comment.
Paperwork Reduction Act.
This final rule does not involve a collection of information. Therefore, the Paperwork Reduction Act, 44 U.S.C. 3501et seq.,
does not apply.
Congressional Review Act (CRA).
This final rule is not a major rule pursuant to the CRA, 5 U.S.C. 801et seq.

AGENCY:
Office of Government Ethics.
ACTION:
Final rule; technical amendment.
SUMMARY:
The U.S. Office of Government Ethics (OGE) is issuing this final rule to update the name of an existing departmental component that was previously designated for purposes of the one-year post-employment conflict of interest restriction for senior employees.
DATES:
Effective October 15, 2026.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
Kimberly L. Sikora Panza, Associate Counsel; Telephone: 202-482-9300; Email:
usoge@oge.gov.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
I. Substantive Discussion; Revision of Existing Departmental Component
The Director of OGE (Director) is authorized by 18 U.S.C. 207(h) to designate distinct and separate departmental or agency components in the executive branch for purposes of 18 U.S.C. 207(c), the one-year post-employment conflict of interest restriction for senior employees. Under 18 U.S.C. 207(h)(2), component designations do not apply to persons employed at a rate of pay specified in or fixed according to subchapter II of 5 U.S.C. chapter 53 (the Executive Schedule). Component designations are listed in appendix B to 5 CFR part 2641.
The representational bar of 18 U.S.C. 207(c) usually extends to the whole of any department or agency in which a former senior employee served in any capacity during the year prior to termination from a senior employee position. However, 18 U.S.C. 207(h) provides that whenever the Director “determines that an agency or bureau within a department or agency in the executive branch exercises functions which are distinct and separate from the remaining functions of the department or agency and that there exists no potential for use of undue influence or unfair advantage based on past Government service,” the Director shall by rule designate that agency or bureau as a separate component of that department or agency. As a result, a former senior employee who served in a designated component of a parent department or agency is barred from communicating to or making an appearance before any employee of that component, but is not barred as to any employee of the parent, of another designated component, or of any other agency or bureau of the parent that has not been designated. Likewise, a former senior employee who served in a “parent” department or agency is not barred by 18 U.S.C. 207(c) from making communications to or appearances before any employees of any designated component of that parent, but is barred as to employees of that parent or of other components that have not been separately designated.
The Director regularly reviews the component designations listed in appendix B to part 2641, and in consultation with the department or agency concerned, makes adjustments as are necessary. Pursuant to the procedures prescribed in 5 CFR 2641.302(e), the Department of Transportation has requested that OGE revise the name of one component currently listed in appendix B to part 2641. Specifically, the Department of Transportation requested that OGE revise Saint Lawrence Seaway Development Corporation to read “Great Lakes St. Lawrence Seaway Development Corporation.” The revision is requested because the Saint Lawrence Seaway Development Corporation was legally renamed the Great Lakes St. Lawrence Seaway Development Corporation as part of the 2021 Consolidated Appropriations Act (Section 512 of Division AA of P.L. 116-260), signed into law on December 27, 2020. The Department of Transportation advised that there have been no substantive changes to this component, and that the component name update is purely a technical change. OGE is therefore amending the Department of Transportation listing in appendix B to reflect the current name of this component.
The designation of Saint Lawrence Seaway Development Corporation in appendix B to part 2641 was effective as of January 1, 1991.
See56 FR 3961. The component name change being made in this rule, which does not affect the underlying component designation date, is effective on October 15, 2026, the date this rule is published in the
Federal Register
.
II. Matters of Regulatory Procedure
Administrative Procedure Act
Pursuant to 5 U.S.C. 553, as the Acting Director of the Office of Government Ethics, I find that good cause exists for waiving the general requirements for notice of proposed rulemaking, opportunity for public comment, and a 30-day delayed effective date. As the change effectuated by the final rule is a minor, technical amendment to the current regulation, notice and comment is unnecessary. Furthermore, it is important and in the public interest that the component name change, which reflects the current organization of the concerned
( printed page 65450)
department be published in the
Federal Register
and take effect as promptly as possible.
Regulatory Flexibility Act
As Acting Director of the Office of Government Ethics, I certify under the Regulatory Flexibility Act (5 U.S.C. chapter 6) that this rule will not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities because it affects only Federal departments and agencies and current and former Federal employees.
Paperwork Reduction Act
The Paperwork Reduction Act (44 U.S.C. chapter 35) does not apply to this rule because it does not contain information collection requirements that require the approval of the Office of Management and Budget.
Unfunded Mandates Reform Act
For purposes of the Unfunded Mandates Reform Act of 1995 (2 U.S.C. chapter 25, subchapter II), this rule will not significantly or uniquely affect small governments and will not result in increased expenditures by State, local, and tribal governments, in the aggregate, or by the private sector, of $100 million or more (as adjusted for inflation) in any one year.
Congressional Review Act
The rule is not a major rule as defined in 5 U.S.C. chapter 8, Congressional Review of Agency Rulemaking.
Executive Orders 12866 and 13563
In promulgating this rule, the Office of Government Ethics has adhered to the regulatory philosophy and the applicable principles of regulation set forth in Executive Order 12866, Regulatory Planning and Review (58 FR 51735, Oct. 4, 1993) and Executive Order 13563, Improving Regulation and Regulatory Review (76 FR 3821, Jan. 21, 2011). Executive Orders 13563 and 12866 direct agencies to assess all costs and benefits of available regulatory alternatives and, if regulation is necessary, to select the regulatory approaches that maximize net benefits (including economic, environmental, public health and safety effects, distributive impacts, and equity). Executive Order 13563 emphasizes the importance of quantifying both costs and benefits, of reducing costs, of harmonizing rules, and of promoting flexibility.

AGENCY:
Bureau of Transportation Statistics, Office of the Assistant Secretary for Research and Technology, U.S. Department of Transportation.
ACTION:
Final rule; delay of effective date.
SUMMARY:
The U.S. Department of Transportation (Department or DOT) is delaying the effective date of its September 3, 2026 final rule, titled “Cause of Airline Delay and Cancellation Categories under Section 511(b) of the FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024,” until February 1, 2027.
DATES:
The effective date of the final rule published on September 3, 2026 (91 FR 56588) is delayed until February 1, 2027.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
Robert Nazareth, Bureau of Transportation Statistics, U.S. Department of Transportation, 1200 New Jersey Avenue SE, Washington, DC 20590, 202-934-2413,
robert.nazareth@dot.gov
(email). You may also contact Blane Workie, Office of Aviation Consumer Protection, U.S. Department of Transportation, 1200 New Jersey Avenue SE, Washington, DC 20590, 202-366-9342 (phone), 202-366-7152 (fax),
blane.workie@dot.gov
(email).
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
Delay of Effective Date
On September 3, 2026, the Department published a final rule with an effective date of October 19, 2026 to implement the requirements of Section 511(b) of the FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024. That final rule amended an existing Bureau of Transportation Statistics (BTS) reporting regulation at 14 CFR 234.4. Under 14 CFR 234.4, reporting carriers must file a report of the causes of reportable flight cancellations and delays within 15 days of the end of the month for which data are reported.[1]
The September 2026 final rule mandated that ten specific types of events be excluded from the BTS “Air Carrier” causal code for carriers to report delays and cancellations, consistent with statutory requirements. The air carrier code is reserved for circumstances that are within the carrier's control. The final rule created a new reporting category to capture these 10 specific events, ensuring that the data reported to the Department and shared with the traveling public accurately reflects the statutory distinction between carrier-controllable events and the specific exclusions identified by Congress. In the final rule, the Department explained that the rule would require revisions to a BTS information collection under OMB Control No. 2138-0041 and approval by OMB of those revisions.
On September 21, 2026, Airlines for America (A4A) requested that the Department extend the effective date of the final rule, which sets forth when airlines must report under the revised cancellation and delay causal reporting categories, to February 1, 2027 so that the changes to reporting under the final rule would start for flights beginning January 1, 2027.[2]
A4A explained that the requested delay of the effective date would provide necessary additional time for the Department to update the BTS technical reporting directive, which provides reporting instructions to carriers; for industry stakeholders to update their systems to ensure that the data is collected, reported, and ingested properly; and for BTS to update its own systems. A4A also stated that a new calendar year would be the “natural and logical” date for the Department to begin applying the updated categories.
For the reasons requested by A4A, the Department agrees that it is appropriate to delay the effective date of the final rule until February 1, 2027. In particular, the Department agrees that applying the reporting requirement to cancellations and delays starting with the new calendar year will provide clearer information for consumers and industry. In addition, the delayed effective date will provide the Department with additional time to obtain necessary approvals for the revised information collection under the Paperwork Reduction Act.
As noted previously, carriers must submit reports on the causes of flight cancellations and delays to BTS within 15 days of the end of the month for which data are reported. Accordingly, the delay of the effective date for the reporting requirement to February 1, 2027 will apply to the reporting of delays and cancellations of flights occurring on or after January 1, 2027. Airlines must file their reports with BTS for the entire month of January 2027 in a manner reflecting the changes in causal reporting described in the final rule.
Good Cause for This Final Rule
The Administrative Procedure Act provides an exception to its notice-and-comment rulemaking procedures when an agency for good cause finds that the requirement is impracticable, unnecessary, or contrary to the public interest.[3]
The Department's final rule titled “Cause of Airline Delay and Cancellation Categories under Section 511(b) of the FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024” would be effective on October 19, 2026 absent a delay of the rule's effective date. DOT only recently became aware of air carriers' need to delay the final rule. There is not sufficient time to propose and seek comment on the delayed effective date before the rule would have come into effect. Accordingly, notice-and-comment procedures are impracticable because they cannot be completed prior to the rule's scheduled effective date.
Signed in Washington, DC.
Edward Strocko,
Acting Director, Bureau of Transportation Statistics.

AGENCY:
Coast Guard, Department of Homeland Security.
ACTION:
Temporary final rule.
SUMMARY:
The Coast Guard is establishing a temporary safety zone for navigable waters within an area of Lake Michigan in Chicago, IL. The safety zone is needed to protect personnel, vessels, and the marine environment from potential hazards created by the Navy Pier Fireworks and Drone Show. Entry of vessels or persons into this zone is prohibited unless specifically authorized by the Captain of the Port, Sector Lake Michigan or their designated representative.
DATES:
This rule is effective from 9 p.m. through 9:15 p.m. on October 15, 2026.
If you have questions about this rule, call or email Lieutenant Michael Vega, Marine Safety Unit Chicago, U.S. Coast Guard; telephone (206) 815-6711, email
D09-SMB-MSUChicago-WWM@uscg.mil.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
I. Table of Abbreviations
CFR Code of Federal Regulations
COTP Captain of the Port
DHS Department of Homeland Security
FR Federal Register
NPRM Notice of proposed rulemaking
§ Section
U.S.C. United States Code
II. Background and Authority
The Coast Guard received notification that fireworks will be launched from a barge and drones from the pier at Navy Pier at Chicago Harbor in Chicago, IL. The Captain of the Port (COTP) Sector Lake Michigan has determined that potential hazards associated with fireworks and drones are a safety concern for anyone within 800 feet of the fireworks display. Therefore, the COTP is issuing this rule under the authority in 46 U.S.C. 70034, which is needed to protect personnel, vessels, and the marine environment in the navigable waters within the safety zone.
Because of these potential hazards, the Coast Guard is issuing this rule without prior notice and comment. As is authorized by 5 U.S.C. 553(b)(B), the Coast Guard finds that good cause exists for not publishing a notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM) with respect to this rule because it is impracticable. The Coast Guard was notified of this event on September 25, 2026 but we must establish this safety zone by October 15, 2026 to protect personnel, vessels, and the marine environment. Therefore, we do not have enough time to solicit and respond to comments.
For the same reason, the Coast Guard finds that under 5 U.S.C. 553(d)(3), good cause exists for making this rule effective less than 30 days after publication in the
Federal Register
.
III. Discussion of the Rule
This rule establishes a safety zone from 9:00 p.m. through 9:15 p.m. on October 15, 2026. The safety zone will cover all waters in Lake Michigan bounded by the points beginning 41°53′00″ N, 87°36′36″ W, east to 41°53′00″ N, 87°36′11″ W, north to 41°53′28″ N, 87°36′11″ W, west to 41°53′28″ N, 87°36′34″ W, and then south to the point of origin. Vessels and persons will not be allowed to enter the zone during this time, unless authorized by the Captain of the Port.
IV. Regulatory Analyses
We developed this rule after considering numerous statutes and Executive orders related to rulemaking. Below we summarize our analyses based on a number of these statutes and Executive orders.
A. Impact on Small Entities
The regulatory flexibility analysis provisions of the Regulatory Flexibility Act of 1980, 5 U.S.C. 601-612, do not apply to rules that are not subject to notice and comment. Because the Coast Guard has, for good cause, waived the notice and comment requirement that would otherwise apply to this rulemaking, the Regulatory Flexibility Act's flexibility analysis provisions do not apply here.
Under section 213(a) of the Small Business Regulatory Enforcement Fairness Act of 1996 (Pub. L. 104-121), if this rule will affect your small business, organization, or governmental jurisdiction and you have questions, contact the person listed in the
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT
section.
Small businesses may send comments to the Small Business and Agriculture Regulatory Enforcement Ombudsman and the Regional Small Business Regulatory Fairness Boards by calling 1-888-REG-FAIR (1-888-734-3247). The Coast Guard will not retaliate against small entities that question or complain about this rule or any policy or action of the Coast Guard.
B. Collection of Information
This rule will not call for a new collection of information under the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (44 U.S.C. 3501-3520).
C. Federalism and Indian Tribal Governments
We have analyzed this rule under Executive Order 13132, Federalism, and have determined that it is consistent with the fundamental federalism principles and preemption requirements described in that Order.
Also, this rule does not have tribal implications under Executive Order 13175, Consultation and Coordination with Indian Tribal Governments, because it does not have a substantial direct effect on one or more Indian tribes, on the relationship between the Federal Government and Indian tribes, or on the distribution of power and responsibilities between the Federal Government and Indian tribes.
D. Unfunded Mandates Reform Act
As required by The Unfunded Mandates Reform Act of 1995 (2 U.S.C. 1531-1538), the Coast Guard certifies that this rule will not result in an annual expenditure of $100,000,000 or more (adjusted for inflation) by a State, local, or tribal government, in the aggregate, or by the private sector.
E. Environment
We have analyzed this rule under Department of Homeland Security Directive 023-01, Rev. 1, associated implementing instructions, and Environmental Planning COMDTINST 5090.1 (series), which guide the Coast Guard in complying with the National
( printed page 65461)
Environmental Policy Act of 1969 (42 U.S.C. 4321et seq.), and have determined that this action is one of a category of actions that do not individually or cumulatively have a significant effect on the human environment.
This rule is a safety zone. It is categorically excluded from further review under paragraph L60(a) of Appendix A, Table 1 of DHS Instruction Manual 023-01-001-01, Rev. 1. A Record of Environmental Consideration supporting this determination is available in the docket.
